quest.title: Whither Should the Water Flow?
quest.description: Having met with the troupe, you learn two critical members have yet to return. First is Pauleau, who is responsible for completing the script. He is in Poisson.
quest.rewards_formatted: Adventure EXP x525, Mora x38100, Hero's Wit x4, Mystic Enhancement Ore x8

talks.objective: Go to Poisson and look for Pauleau

dialogues.speaker: Lauwick
dialogues.text: If I remember correctly, this is where he's staying.

dialogues.speaker: Pauleau
dialogues.text: Who is it?

dialogues.speaker: Lauwick
dialogues.text: It's me. Is the script ready?

dialogues.speaker: Pauleau
dialogues.text: ...You came all the way here for that?

dialogues.speaker: Lauwick
dialogues.text: Ugh, alright, forget that for now. Just come on out, we've got some great news.

dialogues.speaker: Pauleau
dialogues.text: Hmph, nice try... Look, just gimme some time, okay? I'm just wrapping up this last part of the script. I'll be out once I'm done.

dialogues.speaker: Lauwick
dialogues.text: Okay then. Looking forward to your masterpiece.

dialogues.speaker: Furina
dialogues.text: So... as expected, he's missed the deadline.

dialogues.speaker: Dulphy
dialogues.text: The ending is one of the most important parts of the show...

dialogues.speaker: Dulphy
dialogues.text: Even once he's done, it isn't final until we've all had the chance to read through and make sure we agree on it.

dialogues.speaker: Navia
dialogues.text: Someone told me they'd just seen you in Poisson. I assumed it was a case of mistaken identity, but sure enough, here you are... and Furina, too.

dialogues.speaker: Furina
dialogues.text: Ah... I was wondering if we might run into her...

dialogues.speaker: Navia
dialogues.text: So, you're here for Pauleau? Looks like he could be a while, so feel free to take a stroll around town in the meantime. I've made all the arrangements already.

dialogues.speaker: Lauwick
dialogues.text: Oh, it's okay, we can just wait h—

dialogues.speaker: Dulphy
dialogues.text: Thank you for being so considerate, Miss Navia! That sounds wonderful. We'll take that stroll!

dialogues.speaker: Dulphy
dialogues.text: Get over here, you! How oblivious are you!?

dialogues.speaker: Furina
dialogues.text: How are things in Poisson now? Any better?

dialogues.speaker: Navia
dialogues.text: Things are on the mend, but it's a slow process. Some people may never recover from the trauma they experienced.

dialogues.speaker: Furina
dialogues.text: I'm... sorry to hear that. I wish there was something I could do...

dialogues.speaker: Navia
dialogues.text: Please... Must our conversations take such a depressing turn every time we meet?

dialogues.speaker: Navia
dialogues.text: We all have painful memories, but we don't have to let them cloud everything we do.

dialogues.speaker: Navia
dialogues.text: And if you're trying to make a new start, perhaps it's best if you don't bring up the past all the time.

dialogues.speaker: Furina
dialogues.text: Thank you for your words of comfort. You make a very good point.

dialogues.speaker: Furina
dialogues.text: But for now, at least... I think I should stay with the way I'm feeling for a while longer.

dialogues.speaker: Navia
dialogues.text: It's okay. These things take time. Moving on from a painful experience is easier said than done.

dialogues.speaker: Navia
dialogues.text: Which brings me to why I'm here... I thought you should probably know that not everyone here is ready to forgive and forget after the Hydro Archon's inaction in the face of catastrophe.

dialogues.speaker: Navia
dialogues.text: To avoid upsetting the peace, I told the townspeople that everyone here is a member of the theater troupe... and that you are just an actress playing the role of Furina.

dialogues.speaker: Navia
dialogues.text: It's not a perfect solution, but hopefully it means you won't have to lie low while you're here.

dialogues.speaker: Paimon
dialogues.text: That's so thoughtful of you, Navia!

dialogues.speaker: Navia
dialogues.text: Well, what do you expect? I am the courageous and considerate president of Spina di Rosula, after all, like my father before me.

dialogues.speaker: Navia
dialogues.text: Anyway, that was all. Look after her, now.

response.speaker: Furina
response.text: Off we go then... Let's take a look up there.

response.speaker: Furina
response.text: I don't have any friends that I can be frank and honest with, so maybe she's right. You're the closest thing to friends that I have.

dialogues.speaker: Furina
dialogues.text: I'm so grateful that Miss Navia was so understanding. To be perfectly honest, I didn't know if I was ready to meet her.

dialogues.speaker: Furina
dialogues.text: It's always easiest to just run away from your problems. But that never fixes anything. You can't get around the obstacles without facing them.

dialogues.speaker: Paimon
dialogues.text: So that's why you were nervous when they brought up Poisson...

dialogues.speaker: Furina
dialogues.text: Yeah. I'd be lying if I said I wasn't scared of coming back here.

dialogues.speaker: Furina
dialogues.text: Still, I felt it was something I had to do. As I was saying before, I want to see for myself the things that I never could in the past.

dialogues.speaker: Furina
dialogues.text: I'd be overjoyed if the people here could find it in their hearts to forgive me. But they're more likely to unleash a tirade of vitriol against me, which of course I completely understand and accept.

dialogues.speaker: Player
dialogues.text: I'm sure some people didn't buy Navia's lie.

dialogues.speaker: Furina
dialogues.text: Yeah... I can tell people are watching me.

dialogues.speaker: Furina
dialogues.text: I'm sure some people here see the idea of someone coming to Poisson dressed as the Hydro Archon as extremely disrespectful.

dialogues.speaker: Furina
dialogues.text: I used to be terrified of the gaze of other people, especially when they had suspicion or resentment in their eyes.

dialogues.speaker: Furina
dialogues.text: ...*sigh* I guess I wasn't quite ready for this after all.

dialogues.speaker: Paimon
dialogues.text: Paimon's surprised you're making yourself go through all of this.

choices.text: Maybe you've taken on a bit too much in one go?

response.speaker: Furina
response.text: I can't let myself see only the things I want to see. How would that make me any different from before?

response.speaker: Paimon
response.text: Look... There seems to be a crowd gathering over there.

response.speaker: Player
response.text: They're not staying quiet, either.

response.speaker: Furina
response.text: Probably time we made a move.

response.speaker: Furina
response.text: How about we check out Spina di Rosula's ship? We should have a view of the whole of Poisson from there.

choices.text: Me too. It's not like you.

response.speaker: Furina
response.text: What do you mean by that? You expected me to just keep running and hiding from my responsibility forever?

talks.objective: Continue accompanying Furina as she unwinds

dialogues.speaker: Furina
dialogues.text: I'm sorry, you probably just wanted a relaxing stroll, and here I am dumping all this heavy stuff on you.

dialogues.speaker: Paimon
dialogues.text: We don't mind! It's actually refreshing to see a different side of you.

dialogues.speaker: Furina
dialogues.text: Great. Well, I appreciate your company, so please don't disappear just yet.

dialogues.speaker: Furina
dialogues.text: I don't know whether you can tell, but... the years of suffering and loneliness aren't the only reason I have a hard time facing up to who I used to be.

dialogues.speaker: Furina
dialogues.text: As I stand here by the ship, I can't get the images of the rising water out of my mind...

dialogues.speaker: Furina
dialogues.text: One after another, people were taken by the water... All those treasured lives and memories, washed out of existence in an instant.

dialogues.speaker: Furina
dialogues.text: They thought their god would protect them. They had absolute faith that when disaster struck, a divine power would save them from harm.

dialogues.speaker: Furina
dialogues.text: And all the while, I played my part to perfection to convince them that was true...

dialogues.speaker: Furina
dialogues.text: But then the flood waters finally came. And the "Hydro Archon" did nothing.

dialogues.speaker: Paimon
dialogues.text: You shouldn't look at it like that. You were only doing your duty.

dialogues.speaker: Player
dialogues.text: Don't be so harsh on yourself.

dialogues.speaker: Furina
dialogues.text: I've had to go through so many moments like that for the sake of protecting the truth. As time went on, it got harder and harder to bear, and I became more lonely and isolated.

dialogues.speaker: Furina
dialogues.text: Eventually, I realized I had nothing left except the truth. I became terrified of completely failing in my task, and was haunted by the thought of being left all alone, weeping on my throne.

dialogues.speaker: Furina
dialogues.text: Fortunately, we were able to avoid the worst-case scenario thanks to the help of heroic individuals such as yourselves.

dialogues.speaker: Furina
dialogues.text: Everyone rose to their responsibilities. And I finally regained my freedom...

dialogues.speaker: Furina
dialogues.text: But on some level, freedom also means no longer being needed. I have no further use to people.

dialogues.speaker: Paimon
dialogues.text: Huh. Paimon would've never imagined you'd see it that way.

dialogues.speaker: Player
dialogues.text: Think of your freedom as your reward.

dialogues.speaker: Furina
dialogues.text: Reward?

choices.text: Because now, you can finally speak your heart.

response.speaker: Furina
response.text: ...I guess so.

response.speaker: Furina
response.text: Back then, I didn't even dare to dream about having someone to confide in.

response.speaker: Furina
response.text: I was scared of someone recognizing me for who I truly was, and exposing the secret I swore to protect.

response.speaker: Furina
response.text: "Believe in the Furina you see on stage. She is the one you can trust."

response.speaker: Furina
response.text: I had to keep all my feelings, all my curiosity about life to myself. No-one could be allowed to know...

response.speaker: Furina
response.text: That's what I really meant when I said I'm no good at maintaining relationships.

response.speaker: Paimon
response.text: So that's where you were coming from... Paimon totally thought you were just a bit of a diva at heart.

response.speaker: Furina
response.text: Could you please get off my case!? I don't know what's gotten into you today. I'm making an effort here, you could at least try to do the same.

choices.text: What Paimon meant to say was, she doesn't like to see you so down.

response.speaker: Furina
response.text: I do. I once had nothing but the truth, and now, I'm finally free to live my own life again. And even though I have no idea where I'm going right now...

response.speaker: Furina
response.text: At least the choice is in my hands.

response.speaker: Furina
response.text: Alright, it's about time to head back. Pauleau should have finished the ending by now.

response.speaker: Paimon
response.text: Sure. Okay, let's head back and check it out.

choices.text: Do you feel better, having gotten all this off your chest?
You don't have to be anguished and alone anymore.

dialogues.speaker: Dulphy
dialogues.text: Didn't you say you needed to watch what you eat? You're supposed to be cutting down on fried foods, not wolfing down copious quantities of fish and chips, y'know?

dialogues.speaker: Lauwick
dialogues.text: Ah, c'mon, it's not every day we get to dine at Spina di Rosula's expense... Can you believe how generous she is? I'm not about to pass on free food...

dialogues.speaker: Lauwick
dialogues.text: Anyway, my character doesn't need to be slim and good-looking. That's your job.

dialogues.speaker: Dulphy
dialogues.text: Are you kidding me right now? It's not your character's health I'm worried about! It's yours!

dialogues.speaker: Dulphy
dialogues.text: I've spent my whole life battling the effects of ill health, and it kills me to watch you willingly ruin yours by filling yourself up with junk all the time.

dialogues.speaker: Paimon
dialogues.text: Oh no, looks like they're arguing again.

dialogues.speaker: Paimon
dialogues.text: We're back! Could you maybe put your differences aside for a moment?

dialogues.speaker: Lauwick
dialogues.text: Ah, you're back. We've been enjoying Spina di Rosula's VIP treatment in your stead, hehe.

dialogues.speaker: Lauwick
dialogues.text: Pauleau's nearly done. We shouldn't have to wait too much longer.

dialogues.speaker: Paimon
dialogues.text: Great. So, you were discussing your characters, right? We heard she's playing the oceanid who turns into a human girl — what about you?

dialogues.speaker: Lauwick
dialogues.text: Me? I'm an oceanid, too.

dialogues.speaker: Dulphy
dialogues.text: He was originally supposed to take the form of a crane, but he... ahem, outgrew that role. Well, the costume, at least. So now he's playing the boar instead.

dialogues.speaker: Paimon
dialogues.text: Pff... Sorry, sorry...

dialogues.speaker: Furina
dialogues.text: The boar's not a bad character, actually. He's the one who raises the little oceanid, yes?

dialogues.speaker: Lauwick
dialogues.text: That's right. He has some pretty memorable lines, too, like when he imparts some solemn words of wisdom to the little oceanid:

dialogues.speaker: Lauwick
dialogues.text: "If you become human, you can reveal your secret to no one. You will face suffering and loneliness... Is this truly what you want?"

dialogues.speaker: Paimon
dialogues.text: Wait, that sounds kinda familiar...

dialogues.speaker: Dulphy
dialogues.text: It's the most important line in the whole script. I think it's a symbolic statement about our director's life and legacy.

dialogues.speaker: Dulphy
dialogues.text: She kept quiet about all the trials and tribulations she faced in running our troupe, allowing us to devote ourselves fully to performing.

dialogues.speaker: Dulphy
dialogues.text: It was only after she was gone that we realized how tough her job really was.

dialogues.speaker: Furina
dialogues.text: You mentioned earlier that the troupe was like your "home"...

dialogues.speaker: Dulphy
dialogues.text: Yeah. I was born with an incurable illness, and once my family found out it couldn't be treated, they decided they didn't want me anymore.

dialogues.speaker: Dulphy
dialogues.text: I spent some years taking whatever work I could find and trying to manage my illness with various medicines. But whenever I had a bad flare-up, I'd be lying in an alleyway for days at a time.

dialogues.speaker: Dulphy
dialogues.text: It was like that until the director found me one day. She told me I had a great voice, and asked if I was interested in studying singing from her. I said yes.

dialogues.speaker: Dulphy
dialogues.text: She took me under her wing. Taught me to both sing and act, helped me find Mora for my meds, took care of me when my condition decided to flare up... I know it was all a huge burden on her.

dialogues.speaker: Paimon
dialogues.text: She sounds like a really incredible person.

dialogues.speaker: Lauwick
dialogues.text: She really was. She gave everything she had to her troupe and the people in it. All of us were so proud to call her our director.

dialogues.speaker: Lauwick
dialogues.text: I was a lost child, too, when she found me. As the child of a murderer, my parents weren't around when I was little, so I got sent to an orphanage.

dialogues.speaker: Lauwick
dialogues.text: The other kids were always picking fights with me... They'd say things like, "C'mon, you must be pretty tough if you're the son of a murderer!" It was just to taunt me, though. I was an easy target, and they knew it.

dialogues.speaker: Lauwick
dialogues.text: One day, I got beaten up so bad that I just couldn't take it anymore, so I ran away. I'd lost all faith in humanity by that point. Thought the whole world was out to get me.

dialogues.speaker: Furina
dialogues.text: Hm, let me guess... Fortunately, the next person you ran into was the director.

dialogues.speaker: Lauwick
dialogues.text: Yeah. For the first time in my life, I was somewhere I felt safe, and I promised myself I'd stay here until the day the group parted ways.

dialogues.speaker: Pauleau
dialogues.text: The day you hoped would never come... *sigh* How times change.

dialogues.speaker: Lauwick
dialogues.text: Oh, you're finally done? Get your butt over here, there's someone I need to introduce you to. This is our new artistic consultant, Miss Furina.

dialogues.speaker: Pauleau
dialogues.text: ...Furina? THE Furina? Oh my god! How did you manage to wrangle that!?

dialogues.speaker: Furina
dialogues.text: Please, the honor is all mine. I was profoundly moved to hear about your troupe and your wonderful director. I just wanted to do something to help.

dialogues.speaker: Paimon
dialogues.text: Same here!

dialogues.speaker: Pauleau
dialogues.text: Even so, this is just... wow... I'm sorry. I'll try to calm down. Now, where was I...

dialogues.speaker: Pauleau
dialogues.text: Ah yes, the script, of course! Let me give you a rundown of how the story unfolds in my version of the script.

dialogues.speaker: Pauleau
dialogues.text: I'm sure you're already familiar with the beginning of the story: A little Oceanid decides she wants to become a human, against the wishes of her family.

dialogues.speaker: Pauleau
dialogues.text: She finds love and friendship in the bustling city. But then, disaster strikes...

dialogues.speaker: Pauleau
dialogues.text: The people start to notice that all the fresh water in the surrounding area is slowly disappearing. The soil is becoming arid, plants and flowers are withering, and the people begin to panic.

dialogues.speaker: Pauleau
dialogues.text: The little Oceanid, Clio, and her lover decide to do something about it, and investigate the truth of the matter together.

dialogues.speaker: Pauleau
dialogues.text: In the end, they discover that all the waste and pollution created by humans over the years has caused the fresh water to flee the land, as if driven by a consciousness of its own.

dialogues.speaker: Dulphy
dialogues.text: Consciousness? You mean... the water is sentient?

dialogues.speaker: Furina
dialogues.text: Water as a conscious entity... There's actually quite a few stories that explore this theme.

dialogues.speaker: Pauleau
dialogues.text: Since the little Oceanid is a water spirit, she immediately understands how the water is feeling. She then tells her lover about her true identity, as well as the truth behind the crisis.

dialogues.speaker: Pauleau
dialogues.text: Her lover accepts her for who she is, and works with her to find a way to bring the water back. However, unbeknownst to them, there were some people eavesdropping when she revealed her secret...

dialogues.speaker: Pauleau
dialogues.text: The little Oceanid is accused of being directly responsible for driving the water away, and faces the greatest dilemma of her life...

dialogues.speaker: Furina
dialogues.text: And then...?

dialogues.speaker: Pauleau
dialogues.text: In the end, she makes the brave decision to sacrifice herself to save her lover and the rest of humanity...

dialogues.speaker: Paimon
dialogues.text: Huh? But didn't they all treat Clio like a villain? Why would she want to save them after that?

dialogues.speaker: Pauleau
dialogues.text: Well, she mainly wanted to save her lover, plus everyone who'd stood up for her.

dialogues.speaker: Furina
dialogues.text: Through her love for her human partner, she was able to find an even greater love — one that extended to all of humanity. Surely the biggest strength of Clio's character.

dialogues.speaker: Dulphy
dialogues.text: There's actually something else that bothers me...

dialogues.speaker: Dulphy
dialogues.text: You know the protagonist is supposed to represent the director, right? And she never had the chance to become a hero in our world.

dialogues.speaker: Dulphy
dialogues.text: If we're serious about dedicating this show to her memory, we should make the ending as true-to-life as possible.

dialogues.speaker: Dulphy
dialogues.text: What about if... the little Oceanid is hounded to death by people who hate her, her lover makes sure her secret never gets out, and humanity continues down the path to extinction?

dialogues.speaker: Furina
dialogues.text: ...That sounds like too cruel of an ending to me. And perhaps a little irresponsible to present to the audience.

dialogues.speaker: Pauleau
dialogues.text: That ending would be a perfect mirror to Director Aurelie's death. Both arbitrary and meaningless.

dialogues.speaker: Pauleau
dialogues.text: On the day when she went missing, Director Aurelie had instructed us all — somewhat out the blue — to leave the Court of Fontaine and wait for her outside the city.

dialogues.speaker: Pauleau
dialogues.text: We waited and waited at the rendezvous point, but she never came. By the time we returned to the city, she'd disappeared without a trace.

dialogues.speaker: Pauleau
dialogues.text: We looked for her, the Gardemeks looked for her, but she was nowhere to be found. Increasingly, all the signs seemed to point to her being the latest victim in the serial disappearances case.

dialogues.speaker: Dulphy
dialogues.text: The Director was the kindest soul in the world... Yet she was senselessly sacrificed for the sake of a so-called experiment, by someone who had nothing to do with her at all...

dialogues.speaker: Furina
dialogues.text: Hmm... But doesn't the way she suddenly told you to leave the city suggest that maybe she had some sense of what was about to happen? It almost seems as if she was moving you to safety.

dialogues.speaker: Pauleau
dialogues.text: I've been trying to follow up on that ever since, but all my efforts so far have turned up nothing... Vilmant might know something, but he won't open up to me.

dialogues.speaker: Furina
dialogues.text: Vilmant? The one who's playing the role of the villain?

dialogues.speaker: Lauwick
dialogues.text: Yeah. He's been overwhelmed by grief — I think the director's death hit him hardest of all.

dialogues.speaker: Pauleau
dialogues.text: Grief? Hmph, guilt, more like. Also, I... have a hard time imagining that anyone took it harder than me.

dialogues.speaker: Pauleau
dialogues.text: Because... Well, speaking of the play being true-to-life, I... I was deeply, madly in love with Aurelie.

dialogues.speaker: Dulphy
dialogues.text: What? You... You kept that one quiet...

dialogues.speaker: Pauleau
dialogues.text: It's time to be upfront with you all. No more keeping secrets from each other, we'll never be able to agree on the ending if we can't be honest about how we feel.

dialogues.speaker: Pauleau
dialogues.text: I did tell her how I felt once, but she turned me down pretty much straight away.

dialogues.speaker: Pauleau
dialogues.text: She said that we were all like brothers and sisters to her, and she'd never considered us as potential romantic partners.

dialogues.speaker: Pauleau
dialogues.text: Not that it came as a shock or anything — it was what I was expecting to hear. So I told her I'd always be there for the troupe, and I'd always be there for her.

dialogues.speaker: Pauleau
dialogues.text: I said, maybe one day in the future, when everyone's settled in to their own lives and on the up and up, and managing the troupe no longer required her constant attention...

dialogues.speaker: Pauleau
dialogues.text: Well, maybe then she could... reconsider what she really wanted in her life.

dialogues.speaker: Pauleau
dialogues.text: ...And now, that day will never come.

dialogues.speaker: Lauwick
dialogues.text: Oh, Pauleau...

dialogues.speaker: Pauleau
dialogues.text: So if I'm the one writing this ending, then I'm gonna make sure it does right by Aurelie. I won't let anyone get in the way of that.

dialogues.speaker: Dulphy
dialogues.text: *sigh* In that case, you have to straighten things out with Vilmant once and for all. Face to face.

dialogues.speaker: Dulphy
dialogues.text: We've all had our differences of opinion over the ending, but those two have never seen eye to eye on anything. One of them has to compromise if we're ever going to reach a final decision.

dialogues.speaker: Paimon
dialogues.text: Well, if that's where we're at, looks like it's time to go visit Vilmant.

dialogues.speaker: Furina
dialogues.text: Are you ready to face the truth?

dialogues.speaker: Pauleau
dialogues.text: Honestly? I'm slightly terrified. But for the sake of our final performance, I'll do whatever it takes...

dialogues.speaker: Pauleau
dialogues.text: Funny you should ask, though... You really do get what I'm going through right now...

dialogues.speaker: Furina
dialogues.text: I certainly do.

dialogues.speaker: Furina
dialogues.text: Come on, everyone. Allons-y.

dialogues.speaker: Lauwick
dialogues.text: Ah, there you are. We were just buying some fish. There's a clearance sale right now, and the prices are much better than in the city.

dialogues.speaker: Dulphy
dialogues.text: Who said anything about buying them? You're really gonna carry a huge fish around all day while we're out visiting Pauleau and Vilmant?

dialogues.speaker: Lauwick
dialogues.text: Ah... You're right. We don't have anywhere to put it...

dialogues.speaker: Buraud
dialogues.text: Pressure's on now... We gotta make sure we're fully prepared.

dialogues.speaker: Elain
dialogues.text: You're off to Poisson to find Pauleau, right? Have a safe trip! We'll take care of the troupe while you're gone.
